messages:
oncall-bot: Pager HIGH -> api-generation (eu-west-1). Symptoms: elevated 5xx and tail latency for /v1/generate. Affected customers: enterprise-tier routes. Alert link: https://ops.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-17690056

Alex: I'm primary. Kicking off triage: 1) check LB 5xx distribution 2) HPA and pod CPU 3) KV cache miss patterns. Maria you're secondary — can you take pod-side checks and draining plan?

Maria: Acknowledged. I'll check pod logs and KV eviction traces. Starting tail on model-serving pods.

Maria: Logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T22:08:01Z pod/model-b-03 app: kv-evict count=78 miss_ratio=0.62 cpu=86%
2026-03-15T22:08:05Z pod/model-b-07 app: http 500 "kvcache: timeout"
```

Sam: Posting runbooks: surge response -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/response-surge ; drainage + eviction playbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash . Quick tip: if miss_ratio > 0.5 AND CPU > 75% scale first, then drain.

Li: For fast relief we can patch HPA minReplicas and add regional fallback. Commands:
```
kubectl patch hpa model-serving -n hosted-eu-west -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":5}}'
# route change (console) -> add fallback eu-central weight 25% to routeSet enterprise-gen
```
I can apply HPA patch if agreed.

Jordan: Recommend routing fallback now to reduce error blast radius. I'll stand by to flip policy if we confirm cross-AZ imbalance.

Alex: Agreed - apply HPA patch and add 25% fallback. Maria, identify worst pods and cordon one-by-one. Keep in-flight KV warmup.

Maria: Cordon/drain model-b-03:
```
kubectl cordon pod/model-b-03 -n hosted-eu-west
kubectl exec -n hosted-eu-west pod/model-b-03 -- /app/drain.sh --grace 45
kubectl delete pod/model-b-03 -n hosted-eu-west
```
I'll wait for new pod readiness and watch miss_ratio.

devops-bot: Automated event: pod/model-b-03 deleted, pod/model-b-03-new created and Ready at 22:09:12Z. New pod CPU 32% initial, kv miss_ratio dropping.

Maria: New pod shows miss_ratio 0.18 after warmup. Rolling drain next for model-b-07 which had the 500s.

Alex: I'm updating the oncall handoff note: I'll remain primary for 20 minutes to confirm stable. Maria, you own follow-up ticket and postmortem. Sam, please open ticket and add logs + HPA diff + route-change trace.

Sam: Created ticket INC-17690056-POST (https://tickets.redwood.ai/INC-17690056-POST). Included S3 links to pod logs and HPA patch diff.

Li: Route fallback applied (enterprise-gen -> eu-central-1 25% fallback). HPA minReplicas set to 5. Monitor will auto-revert per runbook or we can revert manually.

Maria: After draining model-b-07 we're seeing drops in 5xx. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/hosted-api-eu-west shows p50/p99 improving.

Alex: If anything spikes again, page next-rotation. For the handoff: primary (Alex) holds for 20m, secondary (Maria) will run postmortem and CL: update kv-cache thresholds in runbook. If stable at end of window, I'll hand to oncall rotation.

Sam: Post-incident checklist shared: timeline, HPA patch diff, pod logs, routing change diff, replay snippet. Replay command for reproduction:
```
replay-traffic --window "2026-03-15T22:05:00Z/2026-03-15T22:15:00Z" --route enterprise-gen --out /tmp/replay_inc17690056.log
```

Maria: Adding TODOs to ticket: add regression test for cache-eviction pattern, tune eviction thresholds, autoscaler burst policy. Will submit PR to runbook.

oncall-bot: Auto-stability-check scheduled in 30m. If no new alerts, incident will be marked resolved.

Alex: Summary for handoff note (copy to #incidents and ops): start 22:07 UTC, mitigation: HPA patch + pod rolling drain + regional fallback 25%, immediate customer impact reduced. Follow-ups: Maria to own RCA, Sam to attach artifacts, Li to review HPA policy. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
